coverage: Pier & Point covers four sites on San Francisco's central waterfront: Mission Rock, Mission Bay, Pier 70 and Potrero Power Station. A parcel that is not in this data is outside coverage, not "no activity".

record.name: The Beacon
record.summary: Two residential towers at 250 and 260 King Street, for which the Department of Building Inspection filed new-construction permits in November 2000 (17 stories each; 279 and 307 dwelling units) and recorded both permits with a completed date of 2004-10-06 (a permit closeout date; the permit for 260 King Street now carries the status 'reinstated'); the Assessor roll gives 2004 as year built for the condominium lots at 250 King Street, and two listing sites give 595 residential units and Catellus as developer.

notes.accuracy_caveat: REAL lot geometry -- the outline is Assessor lot 8702011 (19,798 m2, active), so its edges are recorded lot lines, not a surveyed building footprint: it includes any yard, setback or plaza inside the lot and can sit a little off the walls. The lot is condominium-mapped: 614 Assessor lots share this outline (the map lot 8702011 and 613 per-unit lots), so the outline is the building's shared lot, not any one unit. Until 2026-10-12 this record showed the surveyed building footprint (OpenStreetMap (ways 149253142 and 288671185, addr:housename=The Beacon, 250 & 260 King St)); 97% of that outline lies inside the lot and it covered 85% of the lot.

open_questions: Developer is stated only by a listing site (SFHighrises); the Catellus Mission Bay page that was cited for the developer does not mention The Beacon. No primary source read confirms it.
Architect not recorded: Afi + Associates says Skidmore, Owings and Merrill; other attributions seen earlier by the project are unsourced here.

The permits do not use the name 'The Beacon'; the link from the name to 250 and 260 King St rests on the OpenStreetMap addr:housename tag cited in About this shape and on SFHighrises and Afi + Associates, which both give 250 and 260 King St.
No construction start date or opening month found; the permit completed date is a closeout date, not an occupancy date.
The building permit for 260 King St has status 'reinstated' in the Department of Building Inspection data; the meaning is not explained in the data.

The AT&T store at 236 King St is shown as closed on the strength of a Yelp listing that showed it closed as of March 2025 (that is when the listing was seen, not when the store closed); the listing could not be read again (access refused on 2026-10-12) and no other page about the store was found. No opening or closing date is known. The address is assigned to The Beacon by Pier & Point; the listing does not name the building.

Update 2026-10-12, completion year: readable sources conflict. The Department of Building Inspection's data records both new-construction permits as completed on 2004-10-06 and the Assessor roll gives year built 2004 for 593 of 595 lots on King St, while SFHighrises (a listing site) says "Year Built: 2003". A permit closeout can follow occupancy, so 2003 is not ruled out and 2004 is not confirmed as the opening year; the timeline shows only the 2004-10 permit closeout, not a 2003 date.
Unit count of The Beacon: permits propose 279 (250 King St) and 307 (260 King St) dwelling units, 586 together; two listing sites give 595 residential units. The counts are not reconciled.

record.notes: Mixed-use condominium complex at 250 and 260 King St (two apartment-tagged buildings, per OpenStreetMap); the Assessor parcel is condo-mapped across per-unit lots (DataSF Assessor parcel data). A broker's portfolio page (Afi + Associates, read 2026-09-29) describes a 'gourmet grocery store, bank, spa' at the complex; that is a secondary source and does not name the tenants. Architect attribution conflicts between sources (Afi + Associates says Skidmore, Owings and Merrill; earlier research also recorded Brand + Allen Architects and SOM/HKS from sources not cited here) and is not resolved -- not recorded as a fact pending a primary-source confirmation.
